rounce_note: Published values are from Rounce et al. (2016) Table 5, computed on the ASTER GDEM; ours are computed on the Copernicus DEM GLO-30, so absolute SLA angles are not expected to match. The comparison that matters is the binary classification each threshold produces. Our SLA figure is the steepest depression angle within 1 km; Rounce et al. report a single representative SLA value.

events.event: Imja Tsho - depth (m); inventory area 1.738 km2
events.source: Somos-Valenzuela et al. (2014), The Cryosphere 8, 1661-1671: sonar bathymetric survey, September 2012. Note the survey measured a lake of about 1.3 km2; the inventory polygon is a later, larger extent, so our estimate is for a bigger lake than the one measured.

events.event: Imja Tsho - volume (Mm3); inventory area 1.738 km2
events.source: Somos-Valenzuela et al. (2014), same survey. The half-ellipsoid basin assumption is the main reason our volume is high: applying it to the measured depth and 2012 area already gives about 101 Mm3 against the 61.7 Mm3 the bathymetry integrates to.

known_limitations.title: Small Potential Flood Volumes (<5 Mm3) under-detected at 30 m DEM resolution
known_limitations.detail: Only 0/4 of small (<5 Mm3) published PFVs in Fujita et al. (2013) Table 2 are recovered on the 30 m Copernicus DEM vs 15 m ASTER DEM. PFV = 0 is a resolution limit, not a certificate of safety.

known_limitations.title: GloFAS cached grid-cell snapping
known_limitations.detail: 0 of 10 cached river basins have off-mainstem hillslope/tributary cells (flagged with grid_snap_warning=true) until the next live 3x3 mainstem snap runs.

known_limitations.title: Landslide inventory completeness
known_limitations.detail: 0 NASA COOLR and 0 BIPAD records currently loaded (offline cache or upstream endpoints unavailable); displaying 663 undated OpenStreetMap mapped landslide scars only.

known_limitations.title: Active fault surface-trace scope
known_limitations.detail: GEM Global Active Faults Database (Styron & Pagani, 2020; incorporating HimaTibetMap) maps 70 Quaternary surface fault traces in the Nepal region (4 non-fault syncline/anticline folds excluded). It does NOT include continuous mapped surface traces of the Main Boundary Thrust (MBT), Main Central Thrust (MCT), or the buried 3D Main Himalayan Thrust (MHT) megathrust décollement that underlies all of Nepal and generates great Himalayan earthquakes (e.g., 1934 M8.0, 2015 M7.8). Absence of a mapped surface trace does not imply low seismic hazard.

known_limitations.title: Screening tool, not probabilistic forecast or statutory warning
known_limitations.detail: No probability of failure is computed, no 2D hydrodynamic inundation is modelled, and subsurface moraine ice cannot be ruled out from DEMs. Consult DHM (hydrology.gov.np), DMG/NEMRC (seismonepal.gov.np), and NDRRMA/BIPAD (bipadportal.gov.np).
